chunks: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd al-Ubaydi said: Rahim, the mother of al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, who was a free and virtuous woman who had performed Hajj twenty-seven times, informed me from Saeed, the servant of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) - who used to serve him in prison and be sent for his needs - that he was present when he died, just as people die from strength to weakness, until he passed away (peace be upon him).

key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَدٍ: Mother of a child (a female slave who bore her master's child)
key_terms.رَحِيمٌ: Rahim, a female narrator and mother of al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin
key_terms.سَعِيدٌ مَوْلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ: Saeed, the freed servant/client of Abu al-Hasan (Imam al-Kadhim)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Kadhim (a.s.) die in prison according to Shia sources?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the intimate witness of Saeed, the Imam’s servant, who observed the gradual decline of Imam al-Kadhim (AS) in prison, a process often interpreted by Shia scholars as either natural aging or the specific effects of poisoning. The account underscores the dignity of the Imam’s final moments and serves as a key evidence for the martyrdom tradition within the broader context of the Twelve Imams' struggles under Abbasid rule.
